title: Design Real-Time Chat & Voice (Discord)
subtitle: Low-latency guild messaging, WebRTC voice channels, and presence aggregation at scale

stages.title: Stage 1 — Monolithic HTTP Polling
stages.bottleneck: Millions of users polling channels every 1s overloads relational database connections.
stages.narrative:
**Simple Polling MVP.** Users send HTTP POST requests and poll the monolith server to check for new channel messages.

**Bottleneck:** Extremely high CPU overhead and DB connection exhaustion under active channel chatter.

stages.title: Stage 2 — WebSocket Gateway & Guild Router
stages.bottleneck: Routing messages across thousands of active Discord servers (Guilds) with 100K+ concurrent members in a channel.
stages.narrative: **Elixir Gateway & Guild Routing.** Discord uses lightweight Elixir/Erlang processes to maintain millions of persistent WebSocket connections. Incoming channel messages are dispatched to the Guild Router, which fans out updates to all active channel members.

stages.title: Stage 3 — ScyllaDB / Cassandra Channel Storage
stages.bottleneck: Millions of messages sent per minute exhausts MongoDB / SQL disk space. Need fast sequential write archiving.
stages.narrative: **ScyllaDB Channel Partitioning.** Discord switched from MongoDB to ScyllaDB (C++ rewrite of Cassandra) sharded by `channel_id` + Snowflake ID order. Writing channel messages is a fast sequential append to LSM trees on disk.

stages.title: Stage 4 — WebRTC Voice Servers & Global SFUs
stages.bottleneck: Peer-to-peer (P2P) voice call bandwidth degrades when more than 4 users join a voice channel.

nodes.label:
Selective Forwarding Unit
(Media SFU Server Pool)

stages.narrative: **WebRTC Media Server (SFU).** For voice channels, clients connect to dedicated **Selective Forwarding Units (SFUs)** over UDP. Instead of mixing audio server-side, the SFU receives 1 audio stream per speaker and selectively forwards audio streams to listeners.
